content: Olea is a genus that includes approximately 40 species within the family Oleaceae. These species are native to warm temperate and tropical regions, including southern Europe, Africa, southern Asia, and Australasia. Members of this genus are evergreen trees and shrubs characterized by small, opposite, and entire leaves. The fruit produced by these plants is classified as a drupe. The leaves of Olea species contain specialized structures known as trichosclereids. Among the species in this genus, the most significant for human use is Olea europaea, commonly known as the olive tree, which is native to the Mediterranean region. Another notable species is Olea paniculata, a larger tree that can grow to a height of 15–18 meters in the forests of Queensland, Australia. This species produces a hard and durable timber. Additionally, Olea laurifolia, commonly referred to as Black Ironwood, is native to Natal and produces an even harder wood that holds economic importance in South Africa. Certain Olea species serve as food sources for the larvae of specific Lepidoptera species, such as the Double-striped Pug moth. Here is a selection of species within the Olea genus: Olea ambrensis Olea borneensis Olea brachiata Olea capensis (commonly known as Small Ironwood) Olea caudatilimba Olea chimanimani Olea chrysophylla Olea cordatula Olea dioica Olea europaea (commonly known as Olive) Olea exasperata Olea gagnepainii Olea gamblei Olea guangxiensis Olea hainanensis Olea javanica Olea lancea Olea laurifolia (commonly known as Black Ironwood) Olea laxiflora Olea moluccensis Olea neriifolia Olea obovata Olea oleaster (commonly known as Wild-olive) Olea palawanensis Olea paniculata Olea parvilimba Olea polygama Olea rosea Olea rubrovenia Olea salicifolia Olea schliebenii Olea sylvestris Olea tetragonoclada Olea tsoongii Olea undulata Olea welwitschii Olea wightiana Olea woodiana Olea yuennanensis Several species that were previously classified under the Olea genus have since been reclassified into other genera. Examples include: Chionanthus foveolatus (formerly Olea foveolata) Ligustrum compactum var. compactum (formerly Olea compacta) Nestegis cunninghamii (formerly Olea cunninghamii) Noronhia emarginata (formerly Olea emarginata) Osmanthus americanus (formerly Olea americana) Osmanthus heterophyllus (formerly Olea aquifolium or Olea ilicifolia)
